messages:
julia: FYI, AcmePay PROD started seeing 500s and broken embeddings after an automatic regional failover to ap-south-1. Customer reports embedding vectors of length 512 but their pipeline expects 1024. Request IDs: rq_abc123, rq_def456. Started 23:04 UTC. Can someone take a look?

deploy-bot: automated failover triggered: policy=regional-standby, source=eu-west-1, target=ap-south-1, reason=zone-degradation, event_id=evt_2023-11-02_2304

kevin: taking this. quick question — do we know what model variant was actually served on the standby?

julia: quick grep of logs shows: served_model: redwood-neo-lite-v0.9-quant; original pinned model for tenant was redwood-neo-v1.2. See snippet: 
```
served_variant=redwood-neo-lite-v0.9-quant
request_id=rq_abc123
embedding_dim=512
```

omar: that explains the embed dim mismatch. lite-quant variant uses 512 embeddings and a different tokenizer mapping; not a drop-in replacement for v1.2. Routing policy must have allowed any compatible architecture, not strict capability match.

lia: adding more detail: lite variant also uses an alternate tokenizer (byte-bpe) and uses kernel path that strips some control-token sequences. That can cause truncated completions and garbled tokens for prompts that rely on specific token alignments.

kevin: Immediate mitigation: can we force-route AcmePay back to eu-west-1's pool (if healthy) or pin them to redwood-neo-v1.2 until we have a proper compatible standby? Also need to notify billing.

julia: Repro steps I ran from a lab account: 
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-neo-lite-v0.9-quant","input":"invoice #12345"}' 
Response: {"embedding": [...], "embedding_dim":512}  // client expects 1024 -> downstream error

maria: customer also reported a billing spike — they retried on client side when receiving mismatched embedding shapes, resulting in multiple calls. Can finance/sales check if we should credit these retries?

omar: routing note: the fallback rule in eu-west-1 is set to "fallback_to_compatible_architecture" which we misinterpreted; it should be "fallback_to_compatible_capabilities" (embedding dim + tokenizer fingerprint). I'll open a change.

lia: long term fix suggestions: 1) failover guardrails that validate model capability matrix before serving (embed dim, max context, tokenizer-id). 2) add a lightweight capability handshake at connection time that returns model_capabilities in headers so SDKs can reject incompatible fallbacks.

kevin: for now i've applied a temporary override: pinned AcmePay to redwood-neo-v1.2 in eu-west-1 and rolled routing priority up so standby is only used if capability match=true. rm policy id: pol-789 applied at 23:25 UTC.

julia: customer notified and escalated to SEs, they confirmed reduced errors after pin. They still saw ~12% of requests hit lite variant during the 21-minute window before the pin.

maria: filing a refund request for the retry-related overage, tagging billing.

kevin: postmortem action items: (1) change fallback policy semantics (omar), (2) capability handshake + SDK error (lia), (3) add telemetry for "served_variant != pinned_variant" and embed_dim mismatches (kevin). I'll create the incident ticket and assign. :eyes:

omar: opened infra change CR: github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/582 — will block incompatible fallbacks by default.

lia: spike to estimate work on tokenizer handshake will be ready by EOD tomorrow.

julia: thanks all, customer happy for now but wants a root cause and a statement on refunds. I'll follow up with them after the incident ticket is updated. :thumbsup:
